findings.problem: The new wrapper reobserves at entry to transport.send, then delegates to the unchanged locked serializer. That serializer constructs the entire outbound JSON string and unconditionally calls stdin.write. The original absolute clock/abort/closed state is not reobserved between serialization and the native wire effect.

findings.newControlsScope: The positive and queued-negative synthetic cases use a send stub that increments writes immediately and has no serializer. They meaningfully cover the queued-before-send correction, but do not cover a serialization step that crosses the deadline after send-wrapper admission.
findings.originalThirdInstructionPrecision: The original THIRD requested a guard before delegating the write. At8a that closes only the queued/compile portion. The more precise original PRIMARY explicitly required post-serialization native-write admission and warned that wrapping send before the locked serializer leaves this interval open. Both literal original receipts remain unchanged.
findings.requiredNarrowCorrection: In the owned client adapter, retain the pinned wire representation and Promise/cancellation/backpressure/one-close contracts, but reobserve the same absolute clock plus abort/closed/first-failure after bounded outbound serialization and immediately before the actual owned native write. Add native synthetic positive and zero-write controls for expiry during serialization; keep all original source cases and at most3 actual SDK child entries. Update guide transport-write wording to the exact implemented boundary.
